name: Shellac
label: Touch and Go
lede: [[Steve Albini]], the most famous recording engineer in rock, kept the same trio for 32 years, took questions from the crowd mid-set, gave an album to 779 named friends, and saw the last Shellac record come out ten days after he died.

eras.title: A drummer from the 7th Street Entry
eras.text: After Big Black and Rapeman, Albini was a working engineer with no band. A Minneapolis drummer he'd met years earlier and a Boston bassist who moved to Chicago for a studio job turned a few jam sessions into a trio that never changed its line-up.

years.h: A drummer who introduced himself at a Big Black show
years.p: [[Todd Trainer|6c123659-4d26-487f-b156-6b56ffa2bc4c]] of [[Rifle Sport|54f70716-5cef-43e0-99c1-d91b5bd518b4]] and [[Breaking Circus|5f92a6ee-44ef-4eef-8b5b-1bd359b32fd4]] walked up to [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]]'s first Minneapolis show, at the 7th Street Entry. Years later, when Albini came to town to rehearse with Flour, the two started playing together.
years.xp:
Albini told The Wire they began putting together music that seemed like it was actually a band. Trainer told the magazine: "It wasn't until Steve and I started playing together that I was able to really develop my own style."

Trainer was also a one-man band as [[Brick Layer Cake|0e15affb-9c59-4c63-99f0-72e44b92c315]], playing and singing everything himself.

years.big: We could just tell that wasn't gonna be the band.
years.h: Naked Raygun's Camilo Gonzalez tries out on bass
years.p: Camilo Gonzalez of [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] rehearses with Albini and Trainer and plays on Shellac's first single. Albini called him very creative, a great bass player, and couldn't say why it wasn't right.
years.xp: Albini told The Wire he "couldn't really articulate why," but the three of them could tell Gonzalez wasn't going to be the band. The next bassist came from Boston.

years.h: Bob Weston moves to Chicago for a studio job and finds a band
years.p: Albini had recorded the last [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]] album, and bassist [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] moved to Chicago to work at Albini's home studio. Once Weston played with Albini and Trainer, Albini said, it felt like a complete band.
years.xp: Weston told The Wire joining wasn't a foregone conclusion: "I moved out here for the job." Shellac's first gigs were unannounced sets at a Chicago tavern where a friend worked, Albini said. The first announced show was at the Augenblick.

years.h: Albini records Nirvana's In Utero and takes a flat fee
years.p: He engineers [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s third album for a flat fee and no royalties, as he always did. He called himself a recording engineer, never a producer.
years.xp: Before the sessions Albini wrote the band a letter setting out how he worked, including his preference for mixing what he recorded. Wikipedia notes his refusal of royalties meant little passive income even from later hits like Bush's Razorblade Suitcase.

years.h: Two singles on Touch and Go, and a rule against promoting them
years.p: Touch and Go releases The Rude Gesture: A Pictorial History and Uranus, both 7" singles. Uranus carries Wingwalker, for which the band acts out airplane moves on stage.
years.xp: Albini told The Quietus the band decided from the start not to do any promotion. Wingwalker stayed in the set for decades, and Albini improvised its spoken part differently every night.

years.h: Shellac plays Japan, Australia and New Zealand before the US
years.p: A Tokyo show on November 21, 1993 becomes the Live in Tokyo CD on Japan's NUX Organization.
years.xp: Bob Weston told The Wire the thinking was simple: "you're famous, and we're not going to be allowed to learn how to be a band onstage in front of people." Albini was the famous one. Their only US show before the tour was at the Augenblick.

years.h: Albini prices a major-label deal at $4,031.25 a head
years.p: His essay The Problem with Music, in The Baffler No. 5, walks through a hypothetical $250,000 deal in which each band member ends up with $4,031.25.
years.xp: In the same piece he attacked [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]'s move to Geffen. Shellac later ran without advances, managers or booking agents.

eras.title: Second only to Oasis
eras.text: The debut album was a hit by indie standards, and the band did nothing to push it. The next record was pressed for 779 named friends and never sold at all.

years.h: A third single, on Drag City instead of Touch and Go
years.p: The Bird Is the Most Popular Finger comes out on Drag City, the Chicago label.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: At Action Park
years.h: At Action Park reaches No. 2 on the UK indie chart, behind Oasis
years.p: Recorded at Southern in London and Black Box in France, Shellac's debut album sat one spot under [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]], Albini recalled.
years.xp:
Albini's sound came from copper picks, Travis Bean aluminum-neck guitars and a Harmonic Percolator distortion pedal, with Weston's bass and Trainer's huge, spare drumming. The vinyl came out weeks before the CD because of manufacturing delays.

Albini told The Quietus he found Oasis trivial. Fact ranked At Action Park the 18th best album of the 1990s in 2012.

years.h: Albini founds Electrical Audio, a studio built for bands playing live
years.p: His recording business moves from his house toward a Chicago studio meant to record bands live and cheaply. Shellac makes most of its records there.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the founding to 1995; the Chicago building on Belmont Avenue is often dated 1997. By his death Albini's day rate was $900, and he'd keep working unpaid if a band ran out of money.

years.h: 779 friends get The Futurist, each name printed on the sleeve
years.p: Shellac's music for Montreal dance company La La La Human Steps is pressed in 779 copies and given away. Every recipient's name is on the sleeve, with their own circled.
years.xp: The name list was there to stop anyone selling a copy. Albini told The Quietus used copies still went for around $500. Recorded in 1995, the 27-minute piece was never sold in shops.

eras.title: A holiday camp on the English coast
eras.text: Terraform opened with a twelve-minute slow song, and the promo note for 1000 Hurts warned the band had gotten meaner. Then a trio that avoided festivals ended up curating one.

years.h: Terraform opens with twelve minutes of slow
years.p: The first track, Didn't We Deserve a Look at You the Way You Really Are, was called The Long, Slow, Boring Song while the band wrote it.
years.xp: Recorded between 1995 and December 1996. The cover uses space art by Chesley Bonestell. Albini told The Quietus the band was a very selfish enterprise: it made the records it wanted to hear.

years.h: 1000 Hurts comes in a sleeve modeled on an Ampex tape box
years.p: The band's promo note warned that the third album was more mean-spirited than the last, and that Todd sings.
years.xp:
The title plays on 1000 hertz, a calibration tone, and the album opens like an MRL test tape. Albini told The Quietus Canaveral paints JFK as a womanizer, and that listeners often misread Prayer to God as an endorsement.

Jehnny Beth of Savages said 1000 Hurts made her want to play bass.

yt: Shellac at ATP, Camber Sands, April 19, 2002
years.h: Shellac curates All Tomorrow's Parties at a Pontins holiday camp
years.p: Camber Sands, on the English coast, with a band that turned down festivals picking the bill. Wikipedia says [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]]'s turn as curator had talked Albini into playing ATP at all.
years.xp: Albini later said ATP completely changed the festival game, with curated line-ups where everyone was treated well. Shellac took early slots so fans would go see other bands.

eras.title: Questions from the floor
eras.text: Shellac settled into a rhythm: an album every seven years, a yearly trip to Barcelona, and a show that stopped halfway so the crowd could shout questions and the band could shout back.

years.cap: Shellac at Circolo degli Artisti, Rome, 2007
yt: Full set, Primavera Sound (Sala Apolo), Barcelona, 2017
years.h: Primavera Sound makes Shellac a yearly regular
years.p: The band plays Barcelona's Primavera Sound for the first time in 2006 and returns nearly every year after. In 2018 the festival sold merch reading Shellac and 249 More.

years.cap: Bob Weston and Todd Trainer on stage in Sao Paulo, April 2008
q: I did that so I wouldn't have to have ridiculous stage banter.
years.h: Bob Weston takes questions from the crowd mid-set
years.p: It started as a way to fill the gap while Albini retuned after Song of the Minerals. Weston later explained why.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the answers as off-the-cuff and at times jocular. When fans asked to play the drums during the questions, Todd Trainer would hop off his stool and hand over his sticks, The Wire reported.

years.src: Wikipedia: Excellent Italian Greyhound · The Quietus
yt: The End of Radio, live at Primavera Sound, 2018
years.h: Todd Trainer's dog, Uffizi, is on the cover of Excellent Italian Greyhound
years.p: Shellac's first album in seven years is named for Trainer's Italian greyhound. It opens with The End of Radio, half improvised every time they play it.
years.xp: Genuine Lulabelle features uncredited voice work from Ken Nordine and clips of the Homestar Runner character Strong Bad. Spoke opens with a cover of a Rotosound Strings ad from The Who's The Who Sell Out. Mastered at Abbey Road.

years.cap: Albini, Trainer and Weston at All Tomorrow's Parties, May 19, 2007
years.h: Shellac ends the night by taking Todd Trainer's kit apart
years.p: Albini and Weston dismantle the drum kit around Trainer while he keeps playing.
years.xp: The Quietus describes the live show as choreographed, with audience questions during tuning breaks and improvised monologues. Albini put the setlists at about half planned, half chosen on the spot.

yt: Shellac at ATP curated by Shellac, Camber Sands, December 2, 2012
years.h: Ten years on, Shellac curates ATP again
years.p: Ten years after its first turn, Shellac curates All Tomorrow's Parties at Camber Sands, with [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]], [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]], The Ex, [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]], Arcwelder and Oxbow on the bill.

eras.title: One album about surveyors
eras.text: Shellac made one album in this stretch. Albini spent the rest of it telling the music business the internet had solved its problems, apologizing for his younger self, and winning at poker.

yt: Dude, Incredible, live at ATP curated by The Breeders, 2009
years.h: On Dude Incredible, all three members sing, mostly about surveyors
years.p: The fifth album runs a suite of songs about surveyors, the first time all three sing in unison. It reaches No. 85 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: Albini told The Quietus that many early American patriots were surveyors with ground-level knowledge of the land. The chipboard sleeve carries two monkeys shot by Reuters photographer Anton Meres. It was mastered entirely in analog.

yt: Face the Music 2014 keynote: Steve Albini
years.h: Albini tells Melbourne the internet fixed his old complaint
years.p: In a keynote at Melbourne's Face the Music conference, Steve Albini calls the old label system wasteful and praises file-sharing for letting ignored music find listeners.

years.h: Shellac's two John Peel sessions come out as The End of Radio
years.p: Touch and Go releases Shellac's two sessions for BBC DJ [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]], from 1994 and 2004.

years.h: Albini goes public with his regrets
years.p: In a widely shared Twitter thread, he says much of what he said and did from a position of comfort and privilege was awful, and that he regrets it.
years.xp: He wrote that he'd wrongly assumed misogyny and homophobia were solved problems, and regretted treating fascism as a joke. By 2023 he said he was embarrassed by Rapeman's name. [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] said the person he'd become could move her to tears.

years.h: Albini takes a second World Series of Poker bracelet
years.p: Albini wins a $1,500 H.O.R.S.E. event for $196,089, four years after taking a $1,500 stud event for $105,629.

eras.title: Ten days
eras.text: Shellac announced its first album in a decade with no singles, no tour and no advance copies. Albini died ten days before it came out, and the tributes came from the places the band had made its own.

years.big: ...and so we don't send out copies or links to listen to it. Because we don't care.
years.src: Wikipedia: To All Trains · The Wire
years.h: Shellac announces To All Trains and sends nothing to critics
years.p: The first album in ten years is due May 17 on Touch and Go, with no singles and no tour dates. Bob Weston gave The Wire the reason for the silence.
years.xp:
Weston told The Wire the band had never let anyone hear a record before release day in 30 years. The album had been finished for a while, held up by Covid, interrupted tours and pressing-plant delays.

Albini put it more bluntly: "Marketing, which is maybe my most hated thing on earth."

years.h: Steve Albini dies at 61
years.p: A heart attack at his home in Chicago on May 7, 2024. Shellac's line-up hadn't changed in 32 years.
years.xp:
That day, The Wire issue with Shellac on the cover went on sale. Emily Pothast had interviewed all three members on April 15, in what she called the band's final long-form interview.

[[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] dedicated My Hero to him, and [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] played Cosmia in his memory.

years.src: The Wire · Wikipedia: To All Trains
years.h: To All Trains arrives ten days after Albini's death
years.p: Shellac's final album, recorded at Electrical Audio between 2017 and 2022, is named for words Steve Albini saw on an archway at Chicago's Union Station.
years.xp:
Bob Weston shot the archway for the cover; his iPhone photo of himself taking it went on the back. Inside are photos of scrapper trucks, one per member, for the song Scrappers.

It reached No. 12 in Scotland and No. 44 in Germany. AllMusic's Mark Deming said it was impossible to hear without grief.

years.cap: Shellac at Primavera Sound, Barcelona, June 1, 2019
yt: Shellac live at Primavera Sound, Barcelona, June 1, 2019
years.h: Primavera Sound plays To All Trains in Shellac's slot
years.p: The festival fills Shellac's scheduled set with a listening party for the album and renames a stage for Albini.

years.h: Chicago names a block of Belmont Avenue for Albini
years.p: The block of Belmont Avenue at Rockwell, where Electrical Audio stands, becomes Steve Albini Way. [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] and Albini's widow, Heather Whinna, speak at the unveiling.
years.xp: At the afterparty inside the studio, [[Jeff Tweedy|63287966-6021-474a-ba76-edc37a5f1b7c]], [[Fred Armisen|b1bad7e7-18fd-4c1d-9a64-66c3696209ac]] and [[The Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]]' Jon Langford and Sally Timms played as the Electrical Adjacents.
